conventions: A genitive or dative complement keeps the English preposition that realizes its case, even where the ASV strands it and even where an expressed Greek noun standing beside it would license the same English word: ὧν χρείαν ἔχετε → *what things ye have need of* puts *of* on ὧν and leaves χρείαν a bare *need*, as χρῄζετε τούτων ἁπάντων → *of all these things* puts it on ἁπάντων and ἀνθέξεται … ἑνός → *hold to one* puts *to* on ἑνός. Rule 21's support-frame exception is scoped to a supplied frame noun over an accusative and reaches none of these; an accusative object is the contrast and leaves the preposition inside the verb, as ἐπιζητοῦσιν → *seek … after* does.

A supplied English verb in a clause the Greek left elliptical: where the clause writes a subject and nothing else, the verb folds onto that token — ὥσπερ οἱ ἐθνικοί → *as the Gentiles do* gives *do* to ἐθνικοί (rules 56, 68). Where the ASV instead supplies a whole predicate with its own subject and every standing token has already been given its own English, the supplied words are `added` — 6:30's *shall he clothe* resumes ἀμφιέννυσιν, spent on *doth … clothe* in the protasis, over an οὐ, a πολλῷ, a μᾶλλον and a ὑμᾶς that each keep their own word (rules 62, 103).

Where the ASV expands a Greek adverb into a multiword frame containing a supplied generic noun, the head is the word that glosses the adverb's own stem, not the frame's noun: Οὕτως → *After this manner* heads on *this*, the οὑτ- stem being what *this* answers to and *manner of* being the same supplied frame rule 99 never heads on. σήμερον → *this day* and *to day* head on *day* instead, because that Greek word carries a day-element for *day* to gloss and the *this* or *to* is the supplied word. Rule 71's πέραν → *on the other side* and ἐγγύς → *at hand* are not the contrast: there no other English word glosses the lexeme, so the noun is what renders it.

English do-support belongs to the verb whose tense, number and person it carries, never to the negator standing beside it, which keeps only its own *not*: 6:20 *do not break through*, 6:26 *do they reap*, 6:28 *do they spin*, 6:30 *doth … clothe* and 6:32 *do … seek* all keep it inside the verb's unit under rule 9, discontinuously across the negator where the ASV separates them, and rule 17 heads each on the verb word rather than on the auxiliary.
report: One real cross-verse split: the English preposition realizing a genitive complement of *have need*. MAT.6.8 gave the stranded *of* of *what things ye have need of* to the expressed noun χρείαν; MAT.6.32 gives the same *of* to the genitive it governs (ἁπάντων → *of all*), as 6.24 (ἑνός → *to one*), 6.29 (τούτων → *of these*) and 6.25 (τῆς/τοῦ → *than the*) do. Nothing in the source licenses the difference: rule 21's support-frame exception is scoped to a *supplied* frame noun over an accusative, and χρείαν is an expressed noun with a genitive complement. MAT.6.8 is patched to put *of* on ὧν, discontinuous under rule 15, as the corpus's *him of whom* relative units read it; the head stays on *things* (rule 77).

MAT.6.33 (*his kingdom and his righteousness*, one αὐτοῦ) was examined and deliberately left alone. Giving the first *his* to αὐτοῦ and the second to the second article is rule 103's repeated-function-word model — the governing token keeps the first occurrence, the member it introduces takes the second — even though αὐτοῦ stands last in the Greek. The verse's note already records the competing whole-on-αὐτοῦ reading. That is also why the BSB flag on SBLGNT.MAT.6.33.004 is not an error.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error; all seven groups are documented convention differences. 6.1 τό is the articular-infinitive nominalizer (rule 61); the five T-DSN before *secret* and the T-DSM before *Father* are emptied by rule 23 or by the possessive on σου (rule 20); the four T-NSM are second attributive articles before a participle whose head noun is expressed (rule 31); 6.26 εἰς is realized nowhere because the ASV writes *Behold* with a bare object (rule 36); 6.33 τήν as above. No accepted edge was changed to move the rate, and the one patch does not touch a flagged token.

Candidates checked and cleared. do-support is uniform on the verb across 6.20, 6.26, 6.28, 6.30 and 6.32, the negator keeping only *not* (6.20 was reconciled before this pass). Rule 106's case test is applied consistently: an accusative object leaves the particle inside the verb (6.32 *seek … after*, 6.26 *Behold*), an oblique complement takes the preposition itself (6.24, 6.32, and now 6.8). Support-verb frames head uniformly on the complement (6.1 *heed*, 6.2 *trumpet* and *glory*, 6.7 *repetitions*, 6.26 *value*). Articles taking a supplied nominal are uniform under rule 102 (6.3 *hand*, 6.13 *the … one*, 6.27 *the measure of*). Rule 31's verbless-modifier test divides 6.1/6.6/6.9/6.18/6.23 (*who*, *that*) from 6.4/6.6/6.18 (participial, article empty) in the same way every time. The two σήμερον units and the two διορύσσουσιν units agree. οὐδέ/οὔτε/μηδέ each keep whatever English the ASV wrote for them.

No promotions and no amendments. Four candidates were considered and rejected as restatements or as too thin: do-support on the verb restates rule 9's auxiliary clause; the *of*-on-the-genitive holding restates rule 21's genitive arm; the elliptical supplied-verb division is already bounded by rules 56, 62 and 103; and a head rule for an adverb expanded with a supplied frame noun rests on one unit here and would read as counter-evidence against rule 71's πέραν → *on the other side* and ἐγγύς → *at hand*, which head on their supplied nouns. All four are recorded in the conventions log instead.
